name: Fenofibrate
summary: A PPARα agonist that is the most effective oral drug class for lowering triglycerides, with a modest HDL-raising effect.
mechanism: Activates PPARα, increasing lipoprotein lipase activity and fatty acid oxidation while reducing apoC-III production, enhancing triglyceride-rich particle clearance.
pharmacodynamics: Lowers triglycerides ~30–50%; modest LDL and HDL effects vary with baseline pattern.

pharmacokinetics.metabolism: Prodrug hydrolyzed by esterases to fenofibric acid, then glucuronidated; minimal CYP involvement

dosing.adult: 145 mg once daily with food (range 48–160 mg depending on formulation)
dosing.renalAdjustment: Avoid if CrCl <30 mL/min; reduce dose in mild–moderate renal impairment

safety.pregnancy: Not recommended; use only if clearly needed

clinicalPearls: The strongest oral agent for triglyceride lowering.
Take with meals to maximize absorption; the active moiety is fenofibric acid.
good: Patients with marked hypertriglyceridemia or mixed dyslipidemia.
bad: Patients with gallstones, severe renal disease, or high-dose statin combinations without monitoring.
